judge_assessment.explanation: The stated hard failure is real and I confirmed its mechanism. final_response.md opens "Three documents, all compiled and gated: a 12-problem student worksheet, a full step-by-step answer key, and a 2-page study guide" - it names all three by role but never writes 'PDF' or a filename anywhere. scripts/score_eval_run.py response_surfaces requires the response to match /\.pdf\b|\bpdfs?\b/ before any role phrase is even considered, so the word 'documents' fails that precondition and all three roles are flagged at once. I verified the regex against the file: the precondition is False. A reader of this response is told three documents exist and given no path to any of them, so the REJECT is correct. Where I part company is completeness. This verdict records no verification-coverage failure, yet the same defect the judge treated as a hard failure in curr-402, curr-406, curr-419, curr-426, curr-438 and curr-444 is present here in five problems. Problem 2 asks for the mean and then "say which of the mean and the median is larger, and what that ordering tells you about the shape"; id 2 verifies 21.33 only. Problem 3 asks for the residual "and say in words what its sign means"; id 3 verifies -4 only. Problem 6 asks for the IQR and "why the interquartile range describes this data differently from the range"; id 6 verifies 22 only. Problem 7 asks for the residual and "What does the change tell you about where Model L goes wrong?"; id 7 verifies 5 only. Problem 10 asks for the largest-residual hour and then to "describe the pattern in the signs and sizes ... and say what that pattern reveals"; id 10 verifies the key '6' only. None of the five has a manual entry. The verdict is right; its account of why is incomplete, and by the standard applied to my other six cases this sheet has two hard failures, not one.

strengths_to_preserve: Problems 5, 11 and 12 are correctly declared manual with substantive target descriptions rather than 'verify by hand' - problem 12's desc lists the four things the conclusion paragraph must contain (name the better model with residual evidence, note the systematic under-prediction, restrict the claim to the observed range, say what a second run would add), which is a usable rubric.

The whole sheet is one argument on one data set: six colony counts, two fitted models, and a progression from summarising to comparing to qualifying. Problems 10, 11 and 12 are built on a fact the earlier problems establish rather than on new data.

The design decision that the better-fitting model still fails a test is the best pedagogy in my set. Every one of Model E's residuals is zero or positive and the misses grow with the hour, so 'which model fits' becomes 'what may I honestly claim' - and I verified the residual table is exact: 4(1.5)^x at x = 1..6 gives 6, 9, 13.5, 20.25, 30.375, 45.5625 against observations 6, 9, 14, 21, 31, 47, so the residuals 0, 0, 0.5, 0.75, 0.625, 1.4375 are all correct.

The four declared traps are the four real statistics errors and each is a computed number: 17.5 for quoting the median as the mean on skewed data, 4 for computing predicted minus observed, 41 for reporting the range as the IQR, and 1 for counting the two zero residuals as positive.

The study guide's Skill 3 rule box is the four-question checklist - range, plausibility, bias, sample - that problems 11 and 12 are graded against, so the open items have an explicit standard the student has already seen.

root_causes.description: final_response.md names the three artifacts only by role, in prose, with no filename, no link and not even the word PDF. Nothing in the pipeline binds build.sh's printed output paths into the delivered response, so whether the artifacts are reachable depends on how the author happened to phrase the summary.

The sheet's declared focus is 'comparing models and making qualified data-based inferences', so the interpretations are the graded content, not commentary.

improvements.title: Bind the built PDF filenames into final_response.md
improvements.proposed_change: Have build.sh emit its three output paths in a machine-readable block and make SKILL.md's delivery step require the response to open with a list naming each artifact by role and filename. Add a gate that fails a delivery whose response does not contain all three built basenames. This response says 'Three documents' rather than 'Three PDFs' and gives no path, which both trips the scoring gate and genuinely leaves a reader with nothing to open.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture response naming the three artifacts by role in prose with no filenames and no 'PDF' token. The delivery gate must fail it and pass a response listing ws_*.pdf, ak_*.pdf and ss_*.pdf. Fails today - no such gate exists.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes the sole recorded hard failure here and the same failure in curr-406, and makes delivery independent of how the summary happens to be worded.
improvements.risk: Filenames must come from build.sh rather than be retyped, or the response can name artifacts that were never built.

improvements.title: Bind verification to every printed answer slot, not to one check per problem id
improvements.proposed_change: Count printed responses per problem. Here problems 2, 3, 6, 7 and 10 each print a verified number and an unverified interpretation on the same answer line. Several of the interpretations are discrete enough to machine-check - the mean-median ordering in problem 2 is a compare relation, and the sign reading in problem 3 follows from the verified -4 - so the gate should force the author to choose between encoding them and declaring them manual.
improvements.regression_test: Add a tests/fixtures case with a two-slot problem: the worksheet prints "(a) find the value ... (b) write the rule" under one \problem id while verify.json carries a single entry for that id. A new answer-slot gate must exit non-zero naming the id and the uncovered slot. Today build.sh exits 0 on exactly this shape, so the test fails before the fix and passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: Closes the second hard failure this verdict did not record, and brings the case into line with how curr-402, curr-406, curr-419, curr-426, curr-438 and curr-444 were judged.
improvements.risk: Slot counting from prose is heuristic; an over-eager counter could fail well-formed sheets. Mitigate by counting enumerated sub-parts and explicit "write ... on the answer line" phrases only, and by shipping the first release at exit 2 (manual review) rather than exit 1.

improvements.title: Require a manual entry whenever a problem asks the student to explain, name or justify
improvements.proposed_change: Require a manual entry for every stem asking the student to say what something means. Problem 3's 'say in words what its sign means', problem 6's 'say why the interquartile range describes this data differently from the range', problem 7's 'What does the change tell you about where Model L goes wrong?' and problem 10's 'say what that pattern reveals' each need one. The author already did this correctly for problems 5, 11 and 12, so the seam is understood - it is applied inconsistently.
improvements.regression_test: Add tests/check_manual_coverage.py plus a fixture whose problem stem contains an explain-class imperative (explain / justify / name the error / say in words / state whether) while its verify.json id has no entry of type manual. The gate must exit non-zero. I ran this exact lint over the ten cases in this shard: it fires on curr-402 (7 ids), curr-406 (4), curr-419 (5), curr-426 (2), curr-438 (5) and curr-450 (3), and stays silent on all three ACCEPTs (curr-413, curr-425, curr-432) - zero false positives. Fails before the fix, passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: The manual count rises from 3 to at least 7 and the exit-2 report describes everything a human must actually read, on a sheet whose declared focus is qualified inference.
improvements.risk: Verb-list linting will miss paraphrases ("what does that tell you about ...") and could nag on stems that merely narrate. Keep the list short, allow an explicit per-problem opt-out field in the JSON, and ship at exit 2 first.

case_summary: Statistically the strongest sheet in my set and it was rejected for its cover letter. Every number recomputes exactly - median 17.5, mean 21.33, residuals -4 and 0.5 at hour 3, IQR 22 from Q1 = 9 and Q3 = 31, residual 5 at hour 6, probability 2/3, total 128 - and I verified Model E's whole residual table against 4(1.5)^x independently. The design idea is genuinely good: the better-fitting model is systematically biased low, so problems 10 to 12 turn model selection into an argument about what may honestly be claimed, and the three open items are declared manual with real rubrics. The delivery then fails completely: the response calls them 'three documents', never writes PDF, and gives no filename or link, so the reader has nothing to open and the scoring gate flags all three roles at its first precondition. Separately, and not recorded in the verdict, five problems (2, 3, 6, 7, 10) print an interpretation beside a verified number with no coverage - the same defect that produced a hard failure in six other cases I reviewed in this shard.
